title: Owned Edits to a Shared Decision Rule: Learning Private Exceptions as Typed, Gated, Withdrawable Weight Edits
editor_models: none (main mechanism is a deterministic compiler)
unnamed local open-weight models (pilot free-form weight-edit authors)

target_networks.name: compiled rule network, synthetic bench (Construction M)
compiled derating-rule network, real-record bench (Construction I)
trained base 11-17-1 ReLU network with reserved units

domain: federated learning / multi-party rule correction (space component derating and qualification)
tasks_benchmarks: synthetic qualification-screen bench (3 parties, 20 sampled truths x 5 draws)
ECSS-Q-ST-30-11C derating rule with NASA Goddard single-event test rows (compilation only)

headline_result.text: In two pre-registered runs on synthetic data, a typed, gated learner that writes owned weight patches into a compiled rule network scored 96.6% at 30 records per party versus 91.7% for the unchanged rule, non-inferior to seven tuned gradient, federated and pooled baselines.
headline_result.quote: the learner at 30 records per party was non-inferior, within 2 points, to all seven tuned baselines

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 20 sampled truths x 5 record draws per cell (40 truths for trained base); LLM arm single draw

key_claims.claim: Typed declarations laid over a trained base beat the base alone by +5.4 points in a registered test.
key_claims.quote: typed edits over a network trained on shared records beat that network alone by +5.4 points

key_claims.claim: Oracle-tuned private fine-tuning matches the trained-base combination at 30 records, so its accuracy advantage is not established.
key_claims.quote: Well-tuned private fine-tuning, however, matches the trained-base combination at 30 records.

key_claims.claim: A frontier LLM given the records and the rule decided held-out items about as accurately as the patched network (one draw).
key_claims.quote: it decided 347 of 360 probe items correctly, against 348 of 360 for the patched network

key_claims.claim: When local open-weight LLMs authored free-form weight edits, both dropped a term of the rule; the edits fitted every record, so record checks could not catch it.
key_claims.quote: two independent models made the same mistake: each dropped the heritage term, leaving 1,575 errors on the party’s grid.

key_claims.claim: Free-form weight patches can hide thousands of bits with no behavioural change; typed declarations with re-derivation have zero hidden capacity.
key_claims.quote: one patch under the default edit limits hid 7,989 bits with no change in behaviour on any valid input.

key_claims.claim: On a rule-only base the weight form adds nothing over a table of owned exceptions.
key_claims.quote: On a rule-only base, a table of owned exceptions makes the same decisions.

limitations_stated.quote: Every accuracy figure comes from an invented screening world with three parties

limitations_stated.text: Truths were sampled from the typed space, so realisability holds by design.
limitations_stated.quote: The primary cell samples truths from the typed space itself, so realisability (Proposition 7) holds by design

limitations_stated.text: The evidence gate failed its pre-stated shuffled-outcome criterion in both runs.
limitations_stated.quote: proposed far more often in both runs (Section 2.7); that criterion failed.

notes_for_review: Peripheral to WSP: weights are written by a deterministic compiler from typed declarations, not by an LLM; LLM-written weights appear only in a small pilot, where local models authoring free-form edits silently dropped a rule term, which the author uses to argue against free-form LLM edits. Its relevance to the review is the hidden-capacity argument (free-form weight edits can carry thousands of undetectable bits) and the finding that an LLM given the records directly matched the mechanism's accuracy. Statistically careful (pre-registered plans, deviations logged, honest losses), but evidence is synthetic, code is private, and the author has a commercial interest.
